transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-19 15:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Evan Brooks (Redwood AE); Rosa Diaz (Redwood SE); Marcus Lee (Redwood CSM); James Okafor (BlueHarbor Head of Security); Priya Nair (BlueHarbor SRE); Liam Chen (BlueHarbor Product); Noelle Park (BlueHarbor Compliance)

Auto-summary (brief): 48-min weekly pilot govops sync. Discussed S S O flaky token refresh, audit log formatting, data retention for pilot artifacts, and SOC2 evidence requests. Agreed on next steps and owners.

00:00 Evan: All right, good afternoon everyone, thanks for carving time, we wanted to run through the latest pilot telemetry and land on the S S O and retention pieces. Rosa and Marcus from our side are with me.
00:22 James: Hey thanks, yeah quick note — we had one token refresh hiccup yesterday when a user session hit the 2 hour mark, it reauth'd but there was a gap in the audit stream, so that's the big thing for us.
00:38 Rosa: mm-hmm we saw that, thanks for flagging. I dug into the logs this morning, looks like the refresh callback from your IdP returned a 200 but there was a duplicate session id mapping, so the middleware dropped one event, weird.
00:55 Priya: yeah, we saw a hole in Splunk ingestion as well, it was exactly that 23:05 UTC window. Not sure if it's Redwood or our forwarder.
01:12 Evan: understood — first pass: we can add a retry on the refresh callback and also emit an explicit session-terminated event before the refresh to avoid the duplicate id case. We'll include the code snippet in the follow-up.
01:28 Liam: quick question, does that change affect latency on token exchange? Our product folks worry about user-facing lag.
01:36 Rosa: minimal, the retry is async and only for the callback path; we measured <20ms added in our dev sim. The session-terminated event is also very small.
01:49 James: ok that sounds fine.
01:55 Speaker 1: (overlap) can you also show the audit sample — we want to map fields into our SIEM pipeline.
02:05 Rosa: yes, I prepared an export. I'll post a redacted sample in the shared drive after the call. It includes fields: request_id, user_id (hashed), action, model_id, token_count, trace_id, timestamp. Note — the user_id in pilot is hashed with SHA-256 by default, we can k-anon or redact on request.
02:33 Noelle: about PII — we need clear docs on what is retained in the KV cache and in logs, and if PII is ever stored.
02:44 Evan: good spot. By default Redwood's runtime keeps a KV cache for speed but the cache is ephemeral and not persisted to disk in the hosted pilot. For dedicated/private we offer configurable persistence. For the pilot here, we are not persisting P I I, we only store hashed identifiers. We'll add the exact memory retention TTL to the doc.
03:10 Priya: can you explain the difference again between the hosted pilot retention and what a dedicated commit would look like?
03:21 Rosa: sure — hosted: ephemeral KV cache in-memory, audit logs forwarded to your SIEM, configurable retention on our side up to 90 days for the pilot; dedicated: you can opt to route logs to your VPC or on-prem syslog, and control longer retention via your own storage (S3, GCP bucket) plus server-side encryption keys (K M S /H S M).
03:49 James: that K M S wording — can we use our K M S key or is it Redwood-managed?
03:56 Evan: for the pilot, Redwood-managed key is default; we can do a bring-your-own K M S if you go dedicated or private. We will include the steps for integrating your AWS K M S in the follow-up.
04:12 Liam: any SOC thing we should care about right now? Noelle?
04:17 Noelle: for pilot gating we just need a SOC2 summary and proof of audit log integrity, basically a snapshot or a signed log sample. Not a full SOC2 attestation yet, but artifacts that align with the SOC2 control matrix.
04:31 Evan: we have a SOC2 summary pack — I'll send that. It contains scope, controls, and a redacted evidence bundle (screenshots and hashes).
04:40 Priya: great. On the audit logs themselves, what format is Redwood exporting — JSON lines or syslog?
04:47 Rosa: JSON Lines; each line is a JSON object with the fields I mentioned. We also offer a syslog bridge if your SIEM prefers.
04:58 James: would you be able to add a persistent UUID across retries so our SIEM can stitch sessions together?
05:06 Rosa: yes that's doable — we can emit an external_trace_id field that survives retries. We'll make it the same as the request_id by default.
05:18 Evan: quick ops question from Marcus — Marcus?
05:21 Marcus: yeah, we had a customer question re: retention windows during the pilot — can customers request shorter retention for certain datasets? BlueHarbor might want 7-day retention for logs containing test PII.
05:33 Evan: absolutely. For hosted we can set a per-tenant retention override. We'll document the API you can call to set retention to 7 days for a given dataset.
05:45 Noelle: we also want to know how redaction works — is it post-processing in the pipeline or do you redact before logs leave the runtime?
05:54 Rosa: redaction can be both. We support inline redaction rules at the runtime level — regex-based field redaction — and downstream transform jobs for more complex PII removal. For pilot, we suggest inline for the fields you listed.
06:10 Priya: would inline redaction add CPU overhead?
06:14 Rosa: nominal, it's string processing; we've seen ~3-5% CPU increase in extreme regex sets. For normal sets it's negligible.
06:25 James: all right let's talk about the bench results we ran last week — Marcus, you can walk us through.
06:32 Marcus: sure. We ran 2 workloads: chat-heavy (avg seq 512) and short Q&A (avg seq 64). With default batching and no KV cache we sustained ~1200 rps on the pilot cluster. With KV cache enabled and tuned batch window to 25 ms we saw token-per-second cost drop by ~28% and p99 latency drop from 340ms to 220ms.
07:00 Liam: that's promising. For customer-facing we need to ensure no increase in token leakage or cache-related PII retention.
07:08 Rosa: cache keys are derived from hashed prompts and a per-tenant salt; we don't store raw prompts in the cache. We'll show the exact key derivation function in the doc.
07:20 Priya: did you test eviction behavior under memory pressure? We need deterministic eviction to avoid leaking older prompts.
07:28 Marcus: yes — eviction policy is LRU with strict TTL; traces show eviction happens within 2-3 seconds of hitting threshold in our sim.
07:36 James: ok good.
07:38 Evan: earlier you mentioned a gap in the audit stream during token refresh — we'll attach the trace logs and the patch for the retry flow.
07:47 Priya: sounds good. Also, can we have a signed checksum for each day's log bundle to prove integrity? That helps the compliance team.
07:55 Rosa: yes we can emit daily bundles with SHA-256 checksums and S3 object manifest. For the pilot we'll provide signed manifests.
08:06 Noelle: perfect. Next item — access controls. We want RBAC for who can view raw logs in the console — can that be scoped to roles in our S S O?
08:16 Evan: yes, for pilot we support mapping IdP groups to Redwood roles. You can map your BlueHarbor-Infra and BlueHarbor-Compliance groups to different RBAC roles. We'll include a sample mapping file.
08:29 Liam: are audit logs accessible via API? Our product telemetry team wants programmatic access.
08:34 Rosa: yes we expose an audit-logs API endpoint with pagination and filters; returns JSON Lines. Access controlled by token with specific scopes.
08:45 James: about the token — do refresh tokens live on client side only? Concerned about token theft.
08:52 Evan: refresh tokens are short-lived and we rotate them. We also support the rotating refresh tokens via your IdP if needed.
09:01 Priya: ok. Slight tangent — any blockers on pushing the pilot into our staging org?
09:06 Evan: not from our side, we just need the retention window confirmation and the SSO group mapping from you. Once we have those we can route logs to your staging SIEM endpoint.
09:20 James: we'll aim to provide by next Friday.
09:24 Speaker 1: (crosstalk) question about logs size — how much ingested per 1k sessions per day?
09:31 Marcus: approx 2.4GB/day for chat-heavy workloads at current verbosity. We can drop verbosity or sample logs to reduce footprint.
09:42 Noelle: about SOC2 evidence — Evan you said you'll share a doc. What specifically will you include?
09:48 Evan: SOC2 summary, control matrix, redacted audit screenshots illustrating access reviews and incident response playbook, plus a sample signed log bundle. Also a short note on our encryption in transit and at rest.
10:03 Noelle: that should be fine for our compliance gating.
10:08 Rosa: one more technical note: we discovered a corner case where SAML S S O with non-standard nameid formats caused duplicate subject lines; we have a small patch and will post the change.
10:23 Liam: will that require IdP change?
10:26 Rosa: usually not, it's tolerant. We'll add fallback mapping for nameid formats A and B.
10:34 James: what's the plan for final sign-off on the pilot? Timeline?
10:38 Evan: goal is to complete pilot acceptance in 3 weeks — acceptance criteria: no critical security findings, audit logs flowing and stitched into your SIEM, and retention + redaction rules validated. If all green, we can talk Dedicated purchase.
10:55 Priya: 3 weeks is doable. We'll run a final bench on week 3.
11:03 Marcus: to support that, we'll run bench with 1k concurrent chat sessions with KV cache and the proposed retention settings — target date 2026-05-27. We'll share a runbook and invite your SREs.
11:17 Evan: ok, I'll schedule.
11:20 Noelle: any cost delta if we change retention to 7 days?
11:24 Evan: small increase for storage ETL, about 4-6% on the pilot invoicing line item. We'll provide an estimate in the follow up pricing note.
11:38 James: competitor question — we briefly evaluated an in-house inference layer, but the maintenance delta and lack of observability led us to favor Redwood for this pilot.
11:49 Rosa: glad to hear that. We try to make the governance and guarantees straightforward.
11:56 Priya: quick note — for the bench we need a flag to enable full audit verbosity, is that togglable?
12:02 Rosa: yes — there's a verbosity param in the config: low/medium/high. For the bench we recommend medium-high then sample down to low for production to save tokens.
12:18 Liam: can we also toggle the inline redaction rules on/off per dataset for testing?
12:23 Rosa: yep — per-tenant config API. We'll add examples.
12:30 Evan: ok let's capture next steps: I'll send SOC2 summary and K M S integration docs; Rosa will post audit log sample and mapping; Marcus will run bench on 2026-05-27; Priya and Noelle will send retention and SSO group mapping by 2026-05-24.
12:50 James: sounds good. Anything else?
12:53 Noelle: one last ask — can we get a signed NDA addendum allowing deeper log access for compliance folks?
12:59 Evan: yes we have a template addendum, Marcus will circulate.
13:05 Marcus: will do.
13:08 Evan: great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up in the deck and action items.
13:12 Meeting end.
